# Scanning Probe Microscopy System for High Aspect Ratio Nanostructure Mapping

## Overview

The present invention relates to a scanning probe microscopy system specifically designed to map high aspect ratio nanostructures located on a sample surface. Such nanostructures are characterized by having at least one face with a slope angle that exceeds a predetermined threshold, presenting unique challenges for accurate surface characterization that this system is engineered to address.

## Core System Components

The scanning probe microscopy system comprises several essential components that work together to achieve precise nanostructure mapping. At the foundation of the system is a **metrology frame**, which provides a stable reference structure for accurate measurements. Complementing this is a **sample support structure**, which securely holds and positions the sample during the scanning process.

The measurement functionality is provided by a **sensor head**, which contains a probe assembly. This probe is composed of two key elements: a **cantilever** and a **probe tip**. Together, these components form the sensing mechanism responsible for detecting and characterizing the surface features of the sample.

## Scanning and Actuation

To enable the mapping of nanostructures, the system incorporates an **actuator** that scans the probe tip relative to the substrate surface. This controlled movement allows the probe tip to traverse the sample, systematically gathering the data necessary to construct an accurate representation of the nanostructures present on the surface.

## Optimized Probe Tip Orientation

A distinguishing feature of the invention is the deliberate positioning of the probe tip to effectively sense high aspect ratio nanostructures. Rather than being oriented perpendicular to the sample surface, the probe tip is positioned at a **fixed offset angle** relative to the sensor head. As a result, the probe tip is angled with respect to the sample surface. This angular configuration enables the probe to more effectively access and measure the steep faces of high aspect ratio structures, which would otherwise be difficult to characterize using conventionally oriented probes.

## Kinematic Mounting System

To facilitate practical operation and maintenance, the system features a **sensor head carrier** equipped with a mutually cooperating mounting structure. This mounting arrangement forms a **kinematic mount** with at least three contact points. The kinematic mount allows the sensor head to be **detachably mounted**, ensuring both stability during operation and ease of removal or replacement when required. The three-point contact design provides precise, repeatable positioning of the sensor head, which is essential for maintaining measurement accuracy across multiple mounting and dismounting cycles.

# Scanning Probe Microscopy System for High Aspect Ratio Nanostructure Mapping

## Overview

This invention presents a scanning probe microscopy (SPM) system specifically engineered to address the persistent challenge of accurately mapping high aspect ratio nanostructures. Such structures—characterized by their steep sidewalls, deep trenches, and vertical features—have historically proven difficult to characterize using conventional scanning probe techniques, where the geometry of standard probe assemblies limits access to steeply sloped surfaces.

## The Angled Probe Tip Configuration

At the core of this invention is a probe tip mounted at a fixed offset angle relative to the sensor head. Unlike traditional configurations in which the probe extends perpendicular to the sample plane, this angular offset allows the tip to approach and follow surfaces that exceed a predefined threshold angle. By deliberately tilting the probe, the system accommodates the steep gradients typical of high aspect ratio features, enabling the tip to remain in contact with sidewalls and other angled regions that would otherwise fall outside the effective sensing range.

This design directly overcomes a fundamental limitation of standard SPM systems. When a surface slope exceeds a certain angle, a conventionally oriented tip can no longer maintain reliable contact, resulting in distorted or incomplete topographical data. The fixed offset angle ensures that the effective sensing geometry is oriented favorably toward these challenging surfaces, thereby preserving measurement fidelity across the full profile of the nanostructure.

## Detachable Sensor Head and Kinematic Mount

A second defining feature of the system is its detachable sensor head, which is secured to the instrument body by means of a kinematic mount. This mount incorporates at least three contact points, establishing a well-defined and repeatable seating position for the sensor head each time it is installed.

The use of a kinematic mounting arrangement offers two critical advantages. First, it guarantees that the sensor head—and by extension the angled probe tip—returns to precisely the same position and orientation after removal and reattachment. This positional repeatability is essential for maintaining accurate and reliable sensing of angled nanostructures, as even minor variations in probe geometry can compromise measurement accuracy at the nanoscale.

Second, the detachable nature of the sensor head greatly simplifies probe replacement. Probe tips are consumable components subject to wear and occasional damage during operation. By enabling the sensor head to be conveniently detached and reinstalled without complex realignment procedures, the system minimizes downtime and reduces the technical burden associated with routine maintenance.

## Combined Benefits

Together, these features deliver a scanning probe microscopy system that is uniquely suited to the demands of high aspect ratio metrology. The angled probe tip extends the range of measurable surface slopes, while the kinematic mounting system ensures that this capability is delivered with consistent accuracy and practical ease of use. The result is a robust, user-friendly instrument capable of producing precise topographical maps of steeply sloped nanostructures that lie beyond the reach of conventional scanning probe designs.

# Scanning Probe Microscopy System for High Aspect Ratio Nanostructure Measurement

## FIELD AND BACKGROUND SUMMARY

The present invention relates generally to scanning probe microscopy (SPM) systems and, more particularly, to an apparatus and method for accurately measuring the topography and critical dimensions of high aspect ratio nanostructures, such as deep trenches, vias, and vertical sidewalls, that are increasingly prevalent in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), and photonic device fabrication. Conventional scanning probe microscopes employing vertically-oriented probe tips suffer from significant limitations when characterizing such features, as the geometry of a standard tip prevents adequate penetration into narrow, deep structures and introduces substantial measurement artifacts along steep sidewalls, thereby degrading dimensional accuracy and reproducibility. To overcome these deficiencies, the disclosed system incorporates an angled probe tip that is oriented at a predetermined non-perpendicular angle relative to the sample surface, enabling improved access to and faithful reconstruction of steep and undercut features, in combination with a kinematic mount that supports the sensor head to provide highly repeatable, deterministic positioning and rapid, tool-free interchangeability of probe assemblies. Together, these elements cooperate to deliver enhanced measurement fidelity, reduced tip-sample convolution error, and improved throughput for the metrology of high aspect ratio nanostructures, as described in greater detail in the following specification.

# SPM Metrology Tool — Invention Summary

## Overview

The invention relates to a scanning probe microscopy (SPM) metrology tool designed for precision surface measurement and characterization. The apparatus comprises an integrated system of structural, positioning, sensing, and coupling components that together enable high-accuracy, repeatable metrology with a rapidly interchangeable sensor head.

## Key Components

**1. Frame**
A rigid structural frame provides the primary mechanical reference for the tool. The frame supports and spatially registers the sample support and sensor head assembly, maintaining dimensional stability to minimize measurement drift and vibration-induced error during scanning operations.

**2. Sample Support**
A sample support is mounted to the frame and configured to receive and hold a specimen in a defined measurement position. The support establishes a fixed spatial relationship between the sample surface and the sensor head, providing the reference plane against which surface topology is measured.

**3. Sensor Head with Angled Probe**
A sensor head carries a probe oriented at an angle relative to the sample surface (or relative to a reference axis of the head). The angled probe configuration enables measurement access to surface features—including sidewalls, recesses, or high-aspect-ratio structures—that may be difficult to reach with a normally-incident probe. The sensor head detects probe–sample interaction to generate metrology data.

**4. Actuator for Scanning**
An actuator is coupled to effect relative scanning motion between the probe and the sample. The actuator drives displacement along one or more axes, enabling the probe to traverse the sample surface and acquire topographic or metrological data across a region of interest.

**5. Detachable Three-Point Kinematic Mount**
A detachable, three-point kinematic mount couples the sensor head to a carrier. The three-point kinematic constraint defines a unique, repeatable seating position, allowing the sensor head to be removed and reattached—or exchanged for a different head—while restoring precise spatial registration without recalibration. This feature enables rapid interchange of probes/heads while preserving measurement accuracy and positional repeatability.

## Advantages

- Precise and repeatable positional registration via kinematic coupling
- Rapid, tool-free interchange of sensor heads
- Enhanced measurement access through the angled probe geometry
- Structural stability from the rigid frame for low-drift, high-accuracy metrology

# Summary of the Invention

## Overview

The present invention provides systems and methods for metrology of nanostructures characterized by surfaces having slopes that exceed a threshold angle, including substantially vertical or re-entrant sidewalls associated with high aspect ratio (HAR) features. In particular, the invention addresses limitations of conventional scanning probe metrology in which a probe tip is unable to fully access, contact, or accurately characterize steep surface features due to geometric constraints between the tip and the feature being measured.

## Technical Problem Addressed

Conventional atomic force microscopy (AFM) and related scanning probe techniques employ a probe tip that engages a specimen surface along a nominally vertical approach axis. When such a tip encounters a surface region whose local slope exceeds a threshold angle—for example, sidewalls of trenches, vias, fins, or other HAR structures—the tip apex may fail to reach the deepest portions of the feature, may contact the feature along an unintended tip region, or may produce measurement data that does not faithfully represent the true feature geometry. These limitations degrade the accuracy of critical dimension, sidewall angle, and depth measurements.

## Solution Provided

To overcome these limitations, embodiments of the invention utilize a probe tip that is laterally offset relative to a reference axis of the probe assembly. The tip offset positions the tip apex, or an effective measurement portion of the tip, such that it can reach into and engage surface regions having slopes exceeding the threshold angle, including features with aspect ratios that are inaccessible to conventional axially aligned tips.

In representative embodiments, the metrology system comprises:

- **a probe assembly** including a probe tip having a defined offset relative to a reference axis, the offset being selected to enable access to features whose local surface slope exceeds a predetermined threshold angle;

- **a positioning system** configured to translate and/or rotate the probe assembly relative to a specimen, thereby orienting the offset tip to engage high aspect ratio features from a favorable approach direction;

- **a detection system** configured to sense interaction between the offset tip and the specimen surface and to generate corresponding measurement signals; and

- **a controller** configured to determine surface characteristics of the nanostructure, including sidewall geometry, critical dimensions, and depth, based at least in part on the tip offset.

## Advantages

By employing a deliberately offset probe tip, the invention enables accurate characterization of steeply sloped and re-entrant surfaces that are otherwise difficult or impossible to measure using conventional probe geometries. The offset permits the tip to reach the bottoms of narrow, deep features and to engage sidewalls at improved contact angles. In certain embodiments, the controller applies a reconstruction or deconvolution process that accounts for the known tip offset and tip geometry to yield a corrected representation of the true surface profile.

In further embodiments, the threshold angle is defined relative to a surface normal or a scan plane, and the system automatically selects or adjusts the tip offset, approach direction, and/or specimen orientation based on the expected or measured slope of the feature under inspection. The invention thereby provides improved metrology throughput, accuracy, and repeatability for advanced semiconductor and nanofabrication applications involving high aspect ratio structures.

The foregoing summary is illustrative and is not intended to limit the scope of the invention as defined by the claims. Additional features, aspects, and advantages of the invention will become apparent from the following detailed description, drawings, and claims.
